html:
Victor Schoelcher was a French writer and politician who led the campaign that abolished slavery in the French colonies in 1848. A trip to Mexico and Cuba in the 1820s turned him against slavery.

As a minister in the new republic after the revolution of February 1848, he wrote the decree of 27 April that freed about a quarter of a million people. In Martinique, news of the decree reached the enslaved before it took effect, and a rising on 22 May forced the governor to declare freedom at once. Guadeloupe followed days later.

Schoelcher was later elected deputy for Martinique and Guadeloupe. A town in Martinique bears his name, and his ashes lie in the Pantheon in Paris. Many in Martinique now stress the role of the rebels of 22 May as much as his. His decree ended the age of the Code noir.
sum: Victor Schoelcher was a French writer and politician who led the campaign that abolished slavery in the French colonies in 1848. A trip to Mexico and Cuba in the 1820s turned him against slavery.
